title: Eval Hive: score normalization + preboard sprint
content:
Purpose:
A lightweight, operational playbook to: 
- normalize panel scores across interviewers (reduce bias, make hiring decisions repeatable)
- define competency anchors useful for fast calibration sessions
- provide a micro-sprint preboarding checklist (first 10 business days) to improve first-week time-to-contribution

Scope:
- Target roles: IC (E3–E5), Senior IC (E5+), IC manager hires. Separate follow-on doc for exec/leadership interviews.
- Applies to remote and onsite panels; cross-functional panels included.

TL;DR (for hiring managers):
1) Use the 5-dimension scorecard below with the weights shown.
2) Each interviewer must annotate one example sentence (behavioural/technical) tied to each score they give. No numeric-only scores.
3) After panel, collect raw scores and run the median-center step (see "Quick normalization").
4) Convene 20–30 minute calibration sync if panel SD > 1.0 (see calculations).
5) Start preboarding sprint as soon as offer accepted (10 business-day checklist).

Scorecard (single panel form fields):
- Technical competency (0-4) — weight 0.35
- Product sense/problem framing (0-4) — weight 0.20
- System design/architecture (0-4) — weight 0.20 (for senior/infra hires; junior set 0.05)
- Communication & collaboration (0-4) — weight 0.15
- Cultural fit / mission alignment (0-4) — weight 0.10
- Hire recommendation (string: hire / no-hire / strong-hire / needs-discussion)

Competency anchors (quick reference):
0 = no evidence / major gaps (candidate could not reason through basic prompts)
1 = partial / shaky (answers show fragments, needs heavy coaching)
2 = solid baseline (independent contributor level, acceptable with ramp)
3 = strong (above baseline, can mentor juniors)
4 = exceptional (top-of-band; drives technical strategy or exceptional execution examples)

Required annotation rule (enforced in panel notes):
- For any score != 2, attach a 1-line example: "Candidate did X in Y situation, outcome Z". If reviewer writes only a number, HR will request clarification before finalizing. This cuts down numerical inflation/deflation.

Quick normalization (practical, low-friction method):
1) Collect raw numeric scores for each dimension from panel (integers 0–4).
2) Compute interviewer medians across all interviews in the last 4 weeks (this builds an "interviewer baseline"). If interviewer has fewer than 4 interviews in window, fallback to team median.
3) Subtract interviewer median from each raw score to produce a centered score (this removes persistent leniency/strictness).
4) Clip centered score to [-2, +2], then add back global median (usually 2).
5) Multiply by dimension weight, sum to get panel-weighted score.
6) If panel-weighted score difference between top two candidates < 0.15, require calibration meeting and ask for clarifying examples from reviewers.

Rationale note: we intentionally avoid complex z-scores or per-dimension SD scaling because small sample sizes per interviewer make those noisy; median-centering is robust and easy to explain to interviewers.

Calibration meeting checklist (20–30 min):
- Facilitator: hiring manager or people-ops interviewer lead (rotate).
- Agenda: quick walk of top/bottom scoring anchors, ask each reviewer to read their one-line evidence for each non-2 score.
- Deliverable: consensus hire/no-hire and one-line write-up for feedback loop. 
- Use cases that trigger meeting: panel SD > 1.0 on any dimension; conflicting hire recommendations; senior IC where system-design score variance > 1.

Bias & fairness safeguards (operational):
- Blind resume flagging by default for first screen (opt-out by hiring manager).
- Cal team runs monthly bias-spot checks (random sample of 5% of closed reqs).
- People-ops will surface any interviewer with median bias > 0.7 (lenient) or < -0.7 (strict) for a 4-week coaching pulse.

Preboarding micro-sprint (first 10 business days) — owner: people-ops + hiring manager
Day -1 (offer signed):
- Create a starter project ticket in repo (small, read-only task) — owner: hiring manager (JIRA-ONB-XXXX).
- Send welcome packet + 30-minute "what to expect in week 0" video — owner: people-ops.
Day 0 (first day):
- 30 min buddy intro + 60 min setup session (account access, laptop imaging checklist).
- 1-page role readout with three early priorities (shipable outcomes by week 6).
Day 1-3:
- Shadow sessions scheduled with team (2 x 45 min).
- Starter project assigned; reviewer assigned for fast feedback cycle.
Day 4-7:
- Small deliverable due (starter PR or design note).
- 1:1 with manager to set 30/60/90 goals.
Day 8-10:
- Demo to team, feedback retro, finalize first-sprint backlog.
Metrics to track for preboarding sprint: time-to-first-commit, days-to-1st-1:1, checklist completion %. Target: 90% checklist completion by Day 3, first commit within 7 days for engineering roles.

Templates (copy/paste for panels):
- Panel notes header: Role | Candidate | Date | Interviewers
- For each interviewer: Dimension: score | one-line evidence | follow-up question asked
- Hiring manager summary: 3-line recommendation + risk log (top 2 risks)

Open questions / decisions to make (TODOs):
- Should we weight "system design" differently for infra vs product infra vs ML infra? (Ask infra hiring guild).
- Decide SLA for people-ops to nudge reviewers for missing one-line evidence (48 hours?).
- How to integrate off-cycle interviewers (contract, IC mentors) into the interviewer-baseline calculation.

Operational playbook links and quick refs: 
- Confluence: Interviewer training deck (link above)
- Example normalized panel spreadsheet: (internal sheet link placeholder)
- HR escalation flow: email hr-escalations@redwood.ai

Version history / notes: 
- 2025-11-04: initial draft by Aisha Patel (people-ops)
- 2025-11-12: added preboarding micro-sprint and day-by-day checklist (input from Morgan)
- 2025-11-20: added normalization thresholds and calibration triggers (Ethan)

Appendix: quick examples (for calibrators)
Example A: Technical competency 3 -> evidence: "Built high-throughput gRPC service, shipped pagination and retries; benchmarks show 2x throughput improvement"
Example B: Communication 1 -> evidence: "Struggled to articulate tradeoffs during cross-team design question; repeated clarifying Qs multiple times"

Notes to self: keep the form short; pilot for 8 weeks on Eng teams, measure hire quality proxies (ramp time, performance calibration) before rolling company-wide.

End of doc.
